output.brief:
The Kestria buffering problem is almost certainly not the new CDN. Telemetry for 12–25 October shows that only the smart-TV app version 5.2 stalls badly: 5.9% rebuffering, against 0.6–0.7% for every other client. That holds on all three ISPs. Web, mobile and older-version TV sessions are also served by Tessaline, and they are normal. Version 5.2 went live on 9 October, the same day as the CDN cutover, so the two changes were confounded until this breakdown separated them. The handball launch came after the problem began, and match nights are no worse. ISP congestion is ruled out because the same ISPs are fine for other clients.

Recommendation: do not send the breach notice, withhold fees or roll back to Corvane. Do not mute the alert. Instead, revert 5.2's adaptive-streaming behaviour for Kestria, or pause the rollout, and have the TV team fix the regression. Check the 5.2 rollout settings to confirm. Hold the free-month offer. The October price rise also affects cancellations, and the link between buffering and cancellations is unproven. Add app-version breakdowns to the dashboard. I am fairly confident in this diagnosis. The cancellation question is still open.
